chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Regarding the man who prays two rak'at from the prescribed prayer, then forgets and stands before sitting between the two, he said: 'Let him sit as long as he has not bowed, and his prayer is complete. If he does not remember until he bows, let him proceed in his prayer. So when he offers the salutation, he performs two prostrations while he is sitting.'
ai.seo_question: What should a person do if they forget to sit between the two prostrations during prayer?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the distinction between a minor omission (sahw) and a structural break in prayer, establishing that the prayer remains valid if the worshipper proceeds after bowing, requiring only compensatory prostrations. This reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle of facilitating worship by avoiding unnecessary invalidation for simple forgetfulness, a concept rooted in the Prophetic tradition of 'sajdat al-sahw'. The emphasis on performing the prostrations while seated underscores the practical application of ease (rukhas) in daily ritual practice.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Umar Bin Azina, from Al Fuzayl Bin Yasaar,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>

having said regarding the man who prays two Rak’at from the Prescribed ones, then he forgets, so he stands before he had seated between the two. Heasws said: ‘So let him sit for as long as he has not performed Rukū, and he would have completed his Salāt. So if he does not remember until he performs Rukū, so let him accomplish his Salāt. So when he has offered Salām, he should perform Sajdah the two Sujūd (of omission) while he is seated’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘Umar from Fudayl ibn Yasar who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,

about a man who performs two Rak‘at obligatory, then forgets and stands up before sitting between them, has said, ‘He sits down until he has not assumed Ruku‘ (bowing down on one’s knees). His Salah (prayer) is complete. If he does not remember until he assumes Ruku‘, he then continues and after Salam (the phrase of offering greeting of peace) performs two Sajdah (prostration) because of mistake in a sitting position?”
